Canceling out double negations, we reach

example.title: Rewriting Conditional Statement Using the Associative, Commutative, and Absorption Laws

question.explanation:
First, note that \[ \neg P \Rightarrow (P \land Q) \equiv \neg(\neg P) \vee (P \land Q). \]

Canceling out double negations, we reach \[ \neg(\neg P) \vee (P \land Q) \equiv P \vee (P \land Q). \]

Finally, by the absorption law, we have

\[ P \vee (P \land Q) \equiv P. \]

So the given statement is equivalent to $P.$

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $P \Rightarrow Q\equiv eg P \lor Q$
  2. $ eg \left(P \Rightarrow Q ight)\equiv P \land eg Q$
  3. $ eg \left(P \Rightarrow Q ight)\equiv P \lor eg Q$
question.choice5: None of the statements are true.
question.explanation:
Let's examine each of our statements:

  • Statement I is true. Indeed, $P \Rightarrow Q$ is logically equivalent to the disjunction $\neg P \lor Q.$

  • Statement II is true, while statement III is false. From part I, we have the following equivalence: \[ P \Rightarrow Q\equiv \neg P \lor Q \] By negating this statement, we get \[ \neg \left(P \Rightarrow Q\right) \equiv \neg \left(\neg P \lor Q\right). \] Distributing the negation over the disjunction using De Morgan's law, we have \[ \neg \left(\neg P \lor Q\right) \equiv \neg(\neg P) \land \neg Q. \] Canceling out double negation, we reach \[ P \land \neg Q. \] So, $\neg \left(P \Rightarrow Q\right)$ is equivalent to $P \land \neg Q.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

Canceling out double negation, we have

Distributing the negation over the disjunction using De Morgan's law, we reach

\[ eg(R \lor S)\equiv eg R \land eg S. \]

So the given statement is equivalent to $ eg R \land eg S.$

question.text:
$\qquad$ Wear a jacket, or you will get cold.

Which conditional statement is logically equivalent to the disjunctive statement above?
question.choice1: If you don’t wear a jacket, then you will get cold.
question.choice2: If you wear a jacket, then you will get cold.
question.choice3: If you don’t wear a jacket, then you won't get cold.
question.choice4: If you wear a jacket, then you won't get cold.
question.choice5: Wear a jacket, and you won't get cold.
question.explanation:
Let's denote by $A$ and $B$ the following statements:

  • $A{:}$ Wear a jacket.

  • $B{:}$ You will get cold.

Then, our initial statement can be written as $A \lor B,$ which is logically equivalent to

\[ \neg A \Rightarrow B. \]

The negation of $A$ can be written as

  • $\neg A{:}$ You don't wear a jacket.

Therefore, the given statement is logically equivalent to the following:

$\qquad$ If you don't wear a jacket, then you will get cold.
